text:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a small change to rollout/pin metadata to make "stability" an explicit first-class field. reason: we keep adding ad-hoc flags (canary, sticky, soft-expiry) and clients end up reimplementing server fallbacks. want to align semantics across hosted/dedicated/private.

maria: hmm can you summarize the regression-safety and client-compat guarantees?

sam: short: stability tiers are only a guidance surface for routing + fallback ordering. contract: server must never serve a lower-tier model when a higher-tier pin is present for that request unless capacity/failure; clients can opt into strict enforcement. default if omitted = "stable" to preserve current behavior.

trent: sounds reasonable. how does this interact with TTL and soft-expiry today? we have a bunch of pins using pinned_until timestamps.

sam: good Q. proposal: keep pinned_until but add an optional ttl_seconds and stability_tier enum: ["stable","canary","experiment","ephemeral"]. semantics:
```
pin_metadata: {
  model_id: "lh-13b-v2",
  version: "sha256:abc123...",
  stability_tier: "canary",
  ttl_seconds: 3600,   // optional, server-side expiry after last keepalive
  pinned_until: 1699999999 // legacy absolute timestamp (kept for migration)
}
```
server behavior: if pinned_until exists, server treats it as authoritative expiry; if ttl_seconds exists, server exposes it to routing/ops UI and applies soft eviction heuristics.

lina: migration plan? we need a way to convert existing pinned_until values to reasonable defaults for ttl_seconds for Dedicated customers.

sam: plan: 1) read-only ingestion: when we touch a pin, we backfill ttl_seconds = max(0, pinned_until - now) and set stability_tier = "stable" if missing. 2) provide an API param `preserve_legacy_ttl=true` for customers who want exact pinned_until semantics. 3) after 90 days, stop sending pinned_until in new API responses (but keep it in stored records for audits).

aaron: client compatibility: older SDKs just read model_id+version. If we add stability_tier, older clients will ignore it — fine. but we must avoid changing fallback order for those clients. so default server fallback must preserve the current behavior unless client sets `client_enforce_stability=true`.

trent: how do we encode policy for cross-tenant fallbacks? e.g., prefer same-tenant stable over cross-tenant canary?

sam: policy proposal: fallback priority list: 1) same-tenant exact pin 2) same-tenant same-model higher-tier variants 3) global stable pinned variants 4) experimental/canary global variants. We'll codify as an ordered list in config and surface telemetry counters when a fallback happens.

lina: we should add a small observability contract: emit `pin_fallback` event with fields: request_id, requested_pin, chosen_variant, reason_code. that helps SREs debug correctness.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: add schema migration job (backfill ttl_seconds), add server-side toggle `stability_tier_enabled`, surface new field in console, update SDK doc.

maria: another small UX ask — can we allow label aliases? e.g., customers use "prod" vs our "stable". map client labels to canonical tiers on ingest.

sam: yes — mapping table on the control plane, default aliases: {"prod":"stable","beta":"canary"}. will include in RFC text.

trent: edge-case: what if pinned_until is in the past but ttl_seconds is positive due to backfill bug? need invariant checks during read/write.

sam: agreed. add validation: if pinned_until exists and pinned_until < now, treat pin as expired regardless of ttl_seconds unless `force_revive=true` and operator approval.

aaron: one last note on long-term: we might want to collapse this into a small policy DSL later so teams can express richer routing rules. but keep this change intentionally small to avoid cross-team churn.

maria: ok sounds actionable. next steps?

sam: I'll push an RFC addendum with the schema snippet, migration steps, and a minimal rollout toggle. tagging @trent @lina for review. planning to start the backfill job in staging next week.

ops-bot: action: created task INF-4821 "stability_tier pin schema addendum" assigned to sam, due 2026-01-15.
